title: Hiring evidence pocket journal + cohort onboard playbook
summary: Working playbook for running small cohort-based onboarding with an 'evidence pocket' interview journal. Combines lightweight interviewer primers, a multi-signal rubric for early hiring decisions, day-by-day cohort schedule, buddy rotation matrix, and a stripped-down acceptance/handoff checklist. Intended for fast hires in Q1/Q2 2025 where we want consistent ramp signals and better audit trails for offer calibrations.
body:
Context and intent:
This doc is a hybrid working artifact: part interviewer cheat sheet, part candidate evidence log, and part cohort onboarding checklist. Goal: reduce variance across interviewers and make first-90-days signals explicit and visible to hiring committees. Keep it short and usable in meeting prep.

High-level principles (working):
- Evidence first: capture concrete examples, not impressions. Use a short "evidence pocket" entry per interview slot (1-3 bullet examples).
- Time-boxed calibration: weekly 30-min hiring sync for open roles + immediate note normalization for any >1-pt score variance.
- Cohort momentum: run cohort onboarding for hires joining within a 2-week window to make cross-hire calibration and peer support easier.
- Lightweight: this is a living doc; prefer checklists + one-pagers over long forms.

Interviewer primer (copyable to calendar invite):
- 30 minutes total. 5 min intros, 20 min focused questions, 5 min evidence capture.
- Ask for a specific story: context, tradeoffs, measured outcome, what they'd change.
- Score on 3 axes (0-4 each): Technical signal, Problem solving (approach + tradeoffs), Collaboration & communication. Note a single concrete bullet that justifies each axis score.
- No hiring decision in the interview; record only facts and a suggested score. Reserve recommendation to committee.

Evidence pocket template (one-liner entries for each interview):
- candidate: <first last> | interviewer: <name> | slot: <role/area>
- 1-sentence synopsis of answer (what they actually did)
- 1 concrete quote or artifact (command, design snippet, link, repo)
- score vector: Tech=X / Problem=X / Collaboration=X
- follow-ups: 1-2 open questions (quick flags for committee)

Sample evidence pocket entries (examples):
- candidate: Sam Rivera | interviewer: Lina Chen | slot: system design
  - synopsis: proposed sharded KV architecture with durable metadata layer for tenant isolation; considered read/write amplification for hot keys
  - artifact: recommended write-path outline + sample pseudocode for lease; mentioned using MVCC for conflict windows
  - score vector: Tech=3 / Problem=3 / Collaboration=2
  - follow-ups: ask for latency calc for 99th p99 at 20k qps; sample data schema for tenant metadata

Rubric (anchor definitions) — keep short:
- 0: no signal / off-topic / unsafe
- 1: basic familiarity, many gaps, needs high onboarding
- 2: can contribute to well-scoped tasks with mentorship
- 3: broadly independent on role-level responsibilities
- 4: clear senior impact, can lead/mentor and own ambiguity

Score normalization rules (for committee):
- If any axis differs by >=2 between two interviewers, require short 1:1 calibration (10–15m) and re-check evidence pockets before committee vote.
- If average (rounded) across axes is >=3.25 -> strong hire; 2.0–3.24 -> hire with probation/mentorship; <2.0 -> no hire.
- Use "evidence weight" multiplier for recent relevant experience: if candidate shipped same-scale product within last 2 years, +0.25 to Tech axis before rounding (document reason).

Cohort onboarding skeleton (assume 3-6 new hires, cross-functional):
Week 0 — pre-join (people ops):
- send welcome packet + cohort calendar
- ask for hardware/access forms; collect dietary/reasonable accommodations
- assign primary buddy and product buddy

Week 1 — orientation and quick wins:
- Day 1: 09:30 quick exec welcome; 11:00 security & infra setup; 14:00 team intro + team-level 1:1s
- Day 2: product deep-dive + shadow pair on a small triaged task (30–60m)
- Day 3: codebase tour / architecture review (45m) + first day small contributor task (bug or doc)
- Day 4: pairing rotation (buddy switch) + 1:1 mentor check-in
- Day 5: reflect + cohort retro (30m) + clear "first week artifact" submission: candidate adds a short README describing the bug/task they touched

30-day checkpoints:
- Hiring manager: 1:1 weekly, evidence folder review, training plan adjustments
- Coach/buddy: weekly short sync; ensure at least two paired tasks completed
- People Ops: pulse survey at day 14 and day 30 (2 simple Qs: blockers, 1 improvement)

60-day signals (what we look for):
- Delivered at least one meaningful small feature/bugset to prod or documented architecture improvement
- Peer feedback: 3 short peer notes, at least two positive on collaboration or impact
- Clarified learning plan and mentors assigned

90-day decision nodes:
- Offer conversion or full integration decision documented with evidence pockets from the first 90 days (3–5 concrete artifacts).
- If concerns, propose a 30-day remediation with explicit, measurable workback and weekly check-ins.

Buddy rotation matrix (example for 4 engineers):
- week 1: buddy A -> B, B -> C, C -> D, D -> A (shadow matrix)
- week 2: rotate so each new hire sees two different senior owners by end of week 2

Offer calibration evidence pack (for committee):
- one-pager: Role expectations + top 3 hire signals we saw (each with 1-2 evidence pocket bullets)
- links to artifacts (PRs, docs, architecture diagrams) or transcripts/excerpts
- risk log: list of open questions and mitigation plan if hired (mentor assignment, training hours, ramp tasks)

Quick templates (copy into hiring packet):
- "Hiring signal summary" (1-paragraph): \"Candidate shows X, Y; top evidence: bullet list; remaining risks: bullet list. Recommended next step: [hire / hold / no-hire / hire-probation].\"
- "First-week artifact" (for new hire): 200–500 words summary of first contribution + what they learned + 1 improvement suggestion

Interview hygiene checklist for schedulers (people ops / recruiting):
- confirm interviewer has read role one-pager and candidate resume 24h prior
- ensure calendar invites include evidence pocket template link and evaluation rubric
- avoid back-to-back interviewer blocks for candidate (min 15m gap for notes)

Unresolved questions / follow-up items (working):
- do we want a tiny mobile-friendly form for evidence capture (mobile note + sync to candidate folder)? (Action: Marcus prototyping paper form)
- standardize "evidence weight" for career-level adjustments (Action: schedule 15m calibration with hiring leads 2025-03-10)
- adopt a required "first-week artifact" for all engineering hires? (pros: visibility; cons: overhead for PM/infra hires)

Operational notes (short):
- store evidence pockets in folder: Drive > hires > year > role > candidate-lastname-evidence.md (we'll standardize path in docs)
- copy candidate-facing notes (first-week artifact) into their onboarding doc after 2 weeks if manager approves

Appendix: quick interviewer probes by topic (pick 2–3 per slot):
- system design: "walk me through a recent design tradeoff where you chose availability over consistency — why and what did you accept?"
- backend infra: "what's a concrete perf regression you found in a production trace and how did you triage it?"
- product/PM adjacent: "how did you use metrics to decide to cut scope or double down? give numbers."
- collaboration: "tell me about a time you changed your mind after feedback — what convinced you and what happened next?"

Notes to self (Ava):
- Keep examples short; we will run a 1-hour trial with recruiting next week using this playbook and two mock candidate interviews.
- Post-trial: collect feedback in #people-ops and update rubric anchors with concrete examples (target date 2025-03-17).

End of doc (working).
